data.title: Liontrust Shares Won't Catch Peers Until Fund Performance Improves — Market Talk
data.description: Liontrust Asset Management's first-half results look negative as the U.K. fund management group's net revenue margin deteriorated, RBC Capital Markets' Dawid Pych and Sarah Chong write. Adjusted pretax profit missed consensus forecasts by around 20%, as the net revenue margin fell to 50 basis points from 56bps, a worse contraction than guided. The stock continues to appear inexpensive, but the gap to peers won't close until fund performance improves and drives a turnaround in flows, the analysts say. Shares are down 1.7%. (michael.hennessey@wsj.com)

data.title: With foreign aid slashed, Africa must 'own its own future', billionaire Ibrahim says
data.description:
Key points:
  • Foundation says Africa loses around $90 billion annually through capital flight
  • Index shows deterioration across all four major categories in Nigeria, South Africa continues to slide
  • Parts of the continent becoming "ungovernable", Ibrahim says

By Alexander Dziadosz

African governments should use a slump in foreign aid as a chance to take control of their development by cracking down on tax loopholes and investing more domestic resources, British-Sudanese billionaire Mo Ibrahim has told Reuters.

Ibrahim, who made his fortune in telecoms before moving into philanthropy, oversees a foundation that produces an index of African governance examining the state of everything from human rights to armed conflict.

The 2026 index found a slight improvement in overall governance over the past decade, despite a deterioration in security, rule of law and respect for civil rights.

In an interview on Wednesday, Ibrahim said countries along a "conflict arc" extending from the Atlantic through the Sahel towards the Horn of Africa were increasingly becoming "ungovernable".

But he said Africa had resources to improve the situation.

"Africa needs to own its own future and its own economy," Ibrahim said, adding that the responsibility for services such as healthcare and education fell primarily to governments.

"The message here is: Stop relying on the kindness of strangers."

FALLING AID, LIMITED PROGRESS

This year's index showed a "concerning" deterioration across all four of its major categories in Nigeria, Africa's most populous country, while South Africa continued to slide, Ibrahim said.

But continent-wide, gains in economic opportunity and human development helped offset a reduction in security, with improvements in infrastructure, health and education.

Ibrahim said such progress could continue despite "cruel" cuts to foreign assistance.

Globally, overseas development aid from the world's richest nations plunged by 23.1% in 2025, the largest-ever annual reduction, driven by US President Donald Trump's elimination of USAID as a government agency.

"To cut aid in such a severe manner really risks some lives," Ibrahim said. "People are in the middle of treatment ... and then suddenly you take the oxygen mask away."

Africa can compensate for the loss, he said, with serious efforts to tackle capital flight, illicit financial flows and tax manoeuvres utilised by major multinational companies to shift profits to lower-tax jurisdictions.

A 2025 foundation report said that Africa loses an estimated $90 billion a year through capital flight, citing a 2020 UNCTAD report - more than it receives in official development assistance. Almost half of that figure is linked to extractive industries such as gold, it said.

Strengthened tax collection and an end to incentives such as tax holidays would also create significant additional financing, as would directing African pension and sovereign wealth funds to investment on the continent, Ibrahim said.

"If I'm not showing confidence in our own economies, how can we expect other people to come and invest?"

data.title: Everpure Raises FY27 Revenue Outlook After Q3 Beat, But Barclays Cuts P Stock Target On Pricing Concerns
data.description:
Key points:
  • Barclays cut Everpure’s price target to $115 from $132, while maintaining an ‘Equal Weight’ rating, according to The Fly.
  • Everpure raised its fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to $5.2 billion to $5.21 billion from $5.03 billion to $5.07 billion
  • The company’s Q3 gross margin fell to 68% from 72.3% a year earlier.

Everpure (P) reported a better-than-expected third-quarter print and raised its full-year 2027 outlook, but Barclays lowered its price target, flagging the company’s decision to lower product prices at the start of the fourth quarter.

In an earnings call with analysts, Everpure CEO Charles Giancarlo said the company began lowering prices for most of its products at the start of Q4 based on “value engineering and data reduction improvements.”

Barclays highlighted stronger product sales and growing revenue from hyperscaler customers, but slashed Everpure’s price target to $115 from $132, while maintaining an ‘Equal Weight’ rating, according to The Fly. Meanwhile, Raymond James maintained an ‘Outperform’ rating and a $144 price target.

Everpure shares were up about 4.2% at the time of writing.

Everpure Raises FY27 Outlook After Earnings Beat

The company reported a 51% surge in Q3 revenue to $1.46 billion, beating Wall Street’s estimate of $1.33 billion, according to Fiscal.ai. Earnings per share (EPS) came in at $0.86, exceeding consensus estimates of around $0.78.

Everpure raised its fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to $5.2 billion to $5.21 billion from $5.03 billion to $5.07 billion, citing strong demand across its core storage business and increasing contributions from hyperscaler customers.

It also raised its FY2027 operating income guidance to a range of $1.08 billion to $1.09 billion from its previous guidance of $940 million to $960 million.

Gross Margins Decline

Despite the strong results, Everpure’s GAAP gross margin fell to 68% from 72.3% a year earlier. On an earnings call, CEO Charles Giancarlo said product gross margins remained near the lower end of its 65% to 70% target range because of high component costs.

“As stated previously, we continue to operate our core product sales, excluding hyperscale solution sales, at the lower end of our 65%-70% gross margin range, and will do so while these very high semiconductor prices continue,” Giancarlo said.

data.title: NextPlat Announces PharmcoRx Agreement with MedSure Systems to Support Medication Adherence for Retail Medicare Patients in South Florida
data.description:
PharmcoRx Selected for Initial 150-Patient Pilot with South Florida Multispecialty Group Serving Approximately 33,000 Medicare Patients

MedSure Estimates up to 5,000 Group Patients Are Likely Candidates; Parent Organization Serves Approximately 100,000 Additional Medicare Patients, an Expansion Path if the Pilot Succeeds

HALLANDALE BEACH, Fla., Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- NextPlat Corp () ("NextPlat" or the "Company"), a global consumer products and services company providing healthcare and technology solutions through e-commerce and retail channels worldwide, today announced that its PharmcoRx pharmacy subsidiary has signed a Partner Pharmacy Service Agreement with MedSure Systems ("MedSure") to provide prescription fulfillment for a Medicare medication adherence program. The agreement establishes a framework for recurring monthly prescription revenue, with PharmcoRx selected for an initial 150-patient pilot in South Florida.

MedSure is a digital health company whose medication management platform, in-home smart devices and care coordinators help patients take the right medicine at the right time. PharmcoRx will serve as a partner pharmacy for MedSure's new Medicare patient pilot program designed to improve and measure medication adherence. Under the program, PharmcoRx will fill prescriptions in strip-packaged form for use with MedSure's medication management program in the homes of enrolled Medicare patients of a large Multispecialty Group (the "Medical Group") located in South Florida.

"This agreement with MedSure marks an important step forward in our strategy to deliver technology-enabled pharmacy services such as adherence packaging to patients and providers," said David Phipps, Chief Executive Officer and President of NextPlat Corp. "Improving medication adherence is one of the most valuable opportunities in Medicare patient care. By combining MedSure's medication management technology with our pharmacy's strip packaging, at-home delivery services and pharmacist support, we can help patients stay on their prescribed regimens while building a new recurring retail prescription revenue stream."

"The scale of the opportunity in South Florida with the Medical Group is significant, and we look forward to successfully launching the pilot and to potentially expanding the program with MedSure," added Rodney Barreto, Chairman of NextPlat Corp.

Program Highlights:

  • Initial 150-Patient Pilot: MedSure has selected PharmcoRx to participate in an initial 150-patient pilot with a South Florida multispecialty medical group serving approximately 33,000 Medicare patients.
  • Significant Expansion Potential: MedSure estimates that up to 5,000 retail patients from the Medical Group are likely candidates for the program. The group's parent organization serves approximately 100,000 additional Medicare patients, providing a significant potential path to expand the program following a successful pilot.
  • Recurring Prescription Revenue Opportunity: PharmcoRx will fill and deliver each enrolled patient's monthly medication supply, generating a recurring retail prescription revenue stream that is independent of the Company's contracted pharmacy services business.
  • Integrated Care Model: MedSure enrolls patients and coordinates with their physicians, while PharmcoRx manages prescription onboarding, insurance and co-pays, strip packaging, delivery and pharmacist support. The two companies will connect their systems through a secure data integration designed to support timely refills and coordinated care.

"PharmcoRx brings the pharmacy expertise, packaging capability and patient-first service our patients need," commented Justin C. Monger, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of MedSure Systems. "Together, we can help more Medicare patients take their medications as prescribed and stay healthier at home."

About the ProgramMedSure provides a medication management service that combines a smart in-home device, automatic dose reminders and a dedicated Personal MedSure Coordinator who supports each patient and their care team. Patients receive their medications pre-sorted into easy-to-open strip packs, removing the need to fill pill organizers, while physicians gain visibility into each patient's adherence, supporting earlier intervention when patients miss prescribed doses. Improving medication adherence is a priority for Medicare providers and plans, and adherence is a key measure in the Medicare Star Ratings program.

data.title: Nasdaq futures jump on renewed AI optimism ahead of Anthropic's market debut
data.description:
Key points:
  • Futures up: Dow 0.58%, S&P 500 1.16%, Nasdaq 2.08%
  • Anthropic IPO pricing lifts AI-linked stocks
  • Cybersecurity firms up after Palo Alto Networks lifts FY27 forecast

By Medha Singh and Utkarsh Hathi

Nasdaq futures rose more than 2% on Thursday after Anthropic priced its IPO above the marketed range, fueling expectations for a strong market debut and lifting sentiment toward AI-linked stocks after their brutal rout.

Anthropic priced its upsized offering at $83 per share, above its $70 to $78 range, raising $81 billion in the largest listing on record and valuing the AI lab at about $1.5 trillion. It will begin trading on the Nasdaq later in the day.

The listing follows weeks of selling in chipmakers and cloud companies, as investors fretted over stretched valuations, hefty spending on AI infrastructure and the fallout from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's abrupt exit.

"A strong debut is the tonic that the market needs after such a volatile period... it tells us that investor demand is still there," said Fiona Cincotta, senior market analyst at StoneX.

"We can't underestimate the importance of this IPO. It sort of serves as a valuation for the wider AI ecosystem."

Hyperscalers Amazon and Alphabet , also among the investors in the AI startup, added 2.2% and 4.3%, respectively, in premarket trading.

Chipmakers also gained, with Nvidia up 1.7% after falling for five straight sessions through Wednesday, when an upbeat revenue forecast did little to lift sentiment.

Intel , Advanced Micro Devices , Micron , and Marvell rose between 2.7% and 4.3%.

Neoclouds CoreWeave and Nebius gained more than 5% each, while data center-related companies IREN and Applied Digital climbed about 6% each.

At 7:18 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis (YMcv1) were up 293 points, or 0.58%, and S&P 500 E-minis were up 85 points, or 1.16%. Nasdaq 100 E-minis were up 566.5 points, or 2.08%.

The S&P 500 fell for a fifth straight session on Wednesday, with hawkish minutes from the US Federal Reserve's latest meeting also weighing on sentiment.

Nearly all Fed officials saw a need for more rate increases if the economy performed as projected, according to the minutes from the central bank's October policy meeting, while a few warned that inflation could be stickier than anticipated and could call for tighter policy.

Investors will now parse remarks from several Fed officials due later on Thursday.

Traders are pricing in a near-certainty of a 25-basis-point hike at the Fed's December meeting and about an 8% chance of a 50-basis-point move, according to LSEG data.

Among other movers, Palo Alto Networks shares jumped 10.3% after the cybersecurity firm raised its 2027 revenue forecast, helping drive gains of 5% to 6% in peers CrowdStrike , Cloudflare , Okta and Zscaler .

Retail giant Walmart was up 0.9% after it slightly raised its annual targets.
